summary.headline: Apcotex Q1 FY27 revenue hit record Rs 526 crore (+40% YoY) and PAT rose 311% to Rs 79 crore, helped by price realisations and inventory gains.
summary.overview: Management reported record quarterly revenue of Rs 526 crore, up 40% YoY, with operating EBITDA of Rs 117 crore (22.3% margin vs 10.3%) and PAT of Rs 79 crore (15.01% margin vs 5.11%). Volumes fell 10-12% because exports to the MENA region were hit by West Asia disruption, freight costs and logistics issues, while domestic volumes rose about 10%. Management said inventory gains added roughly 2% to EBITDA margin. Working capital rose on higher raw material prices, and net cash fell to about Rs 40 crore from about Rs 70 crore at March 2026 (Q&A noted a figure of about Rs 30 crore).

segments.name: Nitrile latex (NBR/XNBR)
segments.commentary: Margins improved in Q1 versus prior years; management said they were above 15% in Q1 but did not reach that level through FY25-26. NBR is capacity-constrained with ~30% Indian market share, the rest met by imports.

segments.name: Synthetic latex / other products
segments.commentary: Management said margins expanded across all segments in Q1, not just nitrile latex. Company cites about 25 new products added and eight end-industries served.

segments.name: Apco build (small segment)
segments.commentary: Described as growing but still a small part of the business; no numbers given.

guidance_outlook: Average EBITDA margin guidance remains 15-16%; management declined to call Q1 margins sustainable and said it expects some quarters lower and some higher.
NBR capacity expansion expected on stream by Q1 FY28 (possibly April 2028); SB latex and other synthetic latex capex about a couple of months later (around June 2028).

Combined capex of about Rs 220 crore (Rs 130-140 crore for NBR debottlenecking/expansion adding roughly 100% of NBR capacity, rest for synthetic latex). Management expects about Rs 600 crore additional top line, roughly 40% uplift from announced projects.
Decision on a third (stage two) nitrile latex expansion expected in 3-4 months, after watching margins and Asian/Malaysian capacity.
Management expects volumes to rebound quickly once the West Asia conflict eases; said volumes in MENA may not grow near term while oil prices stay high.
capex_capacity: Capex of about Rs 220 crore is in progress; only 15-20% spent so far, mainly advances and civil work. Major equipment deliveries are due in Q3 and Q4 FY27.
NBR debottlenecking/expansion costs Rs 130-140 crore and adds nearly 100% of current NBR capacity; original estimate was Rs 200-250 crore.
Plants run on dual fuel (gas and coal), and each raw material has multiple sources.
Capex so far is self-funded; management expects to take debt in the next couple of quarters.
demand_pricing: Volumes fell 10-12% YoY and QoQ, entirely due to exports; MENA customers were hit by Strait of Hormuz disruption. Domestic volumes rose about 10%.

Realisations were higher in Q1, but management said they started falling late in the quarter as oil and raw material prices eased. It expects another price rise in August-September if crude rises again.
Domestic demand described as strong across paper, construction, rubber goods and others. Ocean freight costs were absorbed by the company on exports.

Competition: no anti-dumping duty in India currently. Management said Europe and the US have no NBR expansion announced; some Asian expansions are coming but expected to be absorbed in three to five years.
Working capital rose because of higher raw material values. Inventory days were unchanged; the increase came from price, not quantity.

qa_highlights.question: How much of the margin came from inventory gains, and what is sustainable?
qa_highlights.answer: Inventory gains added about 2% to EBITDA margin. Management now talks about average margins of 15-16%, not a sustainable level, and said the next few quarters may be lower or higher.

qa_highlights.question: What made the business resilient this quarter?
qa_highlights.answer: Management credited deliberate investments in dual fuel, multiple raw material sources, quick procurement and inventory planning. It said these had been built over several years.

qa_highlights.question: Can throughput double in five years?
qa_highlights.answer: Announced projects should add about Rs 600 crore to top line, roughly 40%. Further doubling depends on market support, and management sees no reason it cannot happen.

qa_highlights.question: Why was the NBR expansion approved now?
qa_highlights.answer: Capex fell to Rs 130-140 crore for almost 100% NBR capacity via debottlenecking, from Rs 200-250 crore earlier. Margins had improved and there is no major NBR expansion globally, so returns were justified.

qa_highlights.question: What is the net cash position and capex spend?
qa_highlights.answer: Net cash of about Rs 40 crore, down from about Rs 70 crore at March, partly due to higher working capital. Only 15-20% of the Rs 220 crore capex has been spent.

qa_highlights.question: Is demand or realisation rising?
qa_highlights.answer: Realisations were higher on average in Q1 but are now falling with oil. Domestic demand is strong across sectors; exports are the main issue, mainly MENA.

risks_watch: Export recovery depends on the West Asia conflict and Strait of Hormuz; management says volumes fall when exports are disrupted.
Q1 margins were lifted by inventory gains and supply tightness; management said the next 3-4 months will show whether margins hold.
Raw material and realisation swings with crude oil; management said net realisation is hard to predict.
Nitrile latex overcapacity in the glove supply chain and possible Asian expansions, including Malaysia (starting July-August 2026).
Working capital and inventory values rise with raw material prices; net cash has fallen.
Q2 seasonality: rains affect construction and footwear demand (the June-August quarter).
summary.management_tone: Confident on operations and the quarter, but cautious on sustainability of margins and timing of nitrile latex expansion. Management repeatedly declined to give normalised margin or volume numbers, saying oil and the war make the outlook hard to call.
key_quotes: We are quite confident of 15%, 16% average margins that I have mentioned before as well.
The NBR will be on stream by Q1 next year as per plan right now.
We have not taken any debt for it yet, but we will be in the next couple of quarters.

financial_highlights.change: down from ~Rs 55 crore in Q4 FY26; Q4 included ~Rs 4 crore one-off impairment and higher repairs
